utterances.speaker: LJUBISAV SIMIC
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Who do you think we should ask --

utterances.speaker: LJUBISAV SIMIC
utterances.text: He was the direct or of the public utilities company, and I don't know why. In fact, he was completely independent in his role as the director. Let me clarify this. If you speak about somebody being subordinate to somebody else, well, this was a legal entity that had its director. Now, I don't know what the relationship was between any of us in the executive board or municipal with director of this legal entity, that's quite pointless because the director had to do jobs that entailed the running of his company. I don't think that Davidovic could issue any orders to him because he was an independent legal entity.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. And I just I didn't use the word subordinate, you did actually in your answer, sir, but be that as it may, tell me who your subordinate --

utterances.speaker: LJUBISAV SIMIC
utterances.text: Well, I used it, and that's why I wanted to correct myself, because it was imprecise and could lead to confusion.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Well, tell me, sir, as you sit here now today under oath, in July of 1995, who were some of your subordinates?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISAV SIMIC
utterances.text: I didn't have any subordinates.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Who did you report to? Who was your superior?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISAV SIMIC
utterances.text: I reported to the assembly. I was one of the 33 or 35 people who were equal there. I was the first among equals because I was the president of the assembly, I chair the sessions, I put forward the agenda, I made sure that the sessions took place and to implement the decisions of the assembly. Let me try and help you understand this because often -- you don't think this is necessary?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: You know, I think we have it, you've explained it and unless the Court really wishes to hear how the structure was and voting went. And I'm quite familiar with how the assembly worked and what the executive having been on a previous case that involved these issues.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Gosnell.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Your Honour, if it pleases the Court, I would respectfully ask that the witness do be allowed to answer the question. And the reason is is that the use of this word subordinate and superior, my learned friend did not define that term, and now it seems that the witness actually wants to explain what he might think by the use of those terms, so I think it's fair enough that he should now explain.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I don't object.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We are not going to stop the witness anyway. At least from what I could gather, it was not our intention to stop him. Yes, Mr. Simic. If you could answer Mr. Ostojic's question. If you need us to read it out to you again, we will do so.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I can continue with my answer because I understood the question at the time, and I could continue. So my role in the assembly was the following: I was the president of the municipal assembly, I was not the mayor. In some municipalities where there were large cities, there were such posts and six years ago after the reforms, we do have the head of the municipality in Bratunac too. According to the last reform, the head of the municipality has the authority that the president of the municipality and the executive board as a collective organ of the executive in the municipality had. At that time, I had the same role as the president of assembly has today, because in addition to the head of a municipality, you also have the president of the municipality assembly, because the president of the assembly again puts forward the agenda, makes sure that the assembly convenes and then implements the decisions. Those were my powers before and those are the powers of the president of the municipality today. At that time I was one among the 33 or 35 deputies who sat in the assembly and I was privileged, if you may call it a privilege, because I Chaired the session, whereas the deputies discussed and passed the conclusions with a majority of votes, and it's at same now, I then was entrusted with implementing the decisions. Making sure that the decisions were implemented and the executive board, a collective body with five or seven members, depending on the municipality, they, the members of the executive board, at that time, comprised of a certain number of people who had some secretariats under them, the secretariat of the economy and so on, and they were appointed to the executive board ex officio and then the assembly appointed the remaining members, and then they would all attend the meetings of the executive board. The president of the executive board convened those meetings, and I played no role in that. I could not affect his work at all. I was able to evaluate his work on the basis of the reports that he brought before the assembly, and that would then debated by all the deputies. He could be praised or criticized for his work, but that's how the work of the president of the executive board was evaluated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Gosnell.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: I am sorry to interrupt, but there is an important transcript issue. Line 48 -- sorry. Page 48, line 23, as I understand it the word "by" should be inserted for the word "and". Implemented by.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Okay. Thank you. Mr. Ostojic.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Is that sufficient for --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: If you are all happy, we are happy with it, at least I am, let's put it like this.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Sir, let me ask you this: Earlier today when we started before the break, I asked you a question regarding Mr. Deronjic and his position as civil commissioner and that he had -- you said on page 39, line 5 that you think mostly his duties had to do with quote "exercising control over the civilian population." And then I asked you, Which do you have in mind, the Muslims, and you said, Yes, yes. Now, when you say exercising control, you are talking about the security of the Muslim population; correct?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISAV SIMIC
utterances.text: Well, probably he knew better than I did, and I did not have an opportunity to ask him in detail about that. I thought that he was smart enough to be able to know what the president ordered him to do and what kind of tasks he was given. And I was not his assistant in this matter at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I know that. Just because I wants to clarify because on July 19th 2007 in the BiH court when you testified last year, you were asked this question by the Prosecutor and you gave this answer, so I just don't know if it's on all fours, and this appears on page 50 -- 58 of 70. It doesn't have a line in the transcript but it's page 58, and I'll let my learned friend catch up, it's on the bottom portion as follows, sir, by the Prosecutor Bulic "you have also said that during the contacts with Miroslav Deronjic, you had the information as you have said that he was in charge of security of the civilians. Witness Simic answer: Yes. Prosecutor Bulic: Which civilians did you have in mind?"

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Can the counsel please slow down.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Prosecutor Bulic: "Which civilians did you have in mind, answer by you, sir, witness Simic, "the Muslims." I just wanted to focus on the word security, do you remember giving that answer under oath in July 19, 2007 in the BiH court?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISAV SIMIC
utterances.text: Yes, and I think that I provided the same answer here. I don't see any reason --

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I thank you for that. If you'd like to say something, sir, I wasn't sure. I didn't mean to cut you off. Did you finish?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISAV SIMIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, I want to go back to this issue of the convoys on the 13th of July in the morning when you came and spoke to Davidovic, and in your transcript in Blagojevic it states on page 7627, and I am focusing primarily on lines 1 through 5 for the moment, so if we could all direct our attention. At that time, sir, you said you were told by Davidovic to go check and then you continued to go to another place and then you saw an officer there, a senior officer, I'm quoting now from lines 2 and 3, you sate "I saw an officer there, a senior officer whom I know now, for whom I know now is called Beara. At the time I didn't know his name." And it goes on, if you'd like to read it, I'm sure you read it in the last few days. What I received, sir, a couple of days ago is a proofing note from the lawyers for Mr. Borovcanin, and they told me in this proofing note that they met with you on the 18th and 20th of October 2008, and they say the following -- and it's on the last page of that two-page document. "Witness did not know who that officer was. He did not ask him, nor did the officer introduce himself." Is that true and accurate, sir?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISAV SIMIC
utterances.text: Well, I don't know what the reference is to. I mentioned a meeting and then I'm getting confused. Let's now clear this up. What meeting are we talking about? What is the date?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I have a proofing note from a meeting from the lawyers who represent Mr. Borovcanin, the 18th and 20th of 2008. They sent us a letter informing us of the contents of the meeting that they had with you, and they shared with us that at that meeting just a few days ago, you said, "Witness did not know who that officer was --"

utterances.speaker: LJUBISAV SIMIC
utterances.text: Excuse me for interrupting you. I just want to say at the meeting during the lawyer, or are you talking about some meeting in Bratunac? That's not clear to me. Are you still talking about the meeting with the lawyer?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I am.

utterances.speaker: LJUBISAV SIMIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, we can continue. Sorry I interrupted you.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: No, no, don't be sorry. Did you, in fact, tell the lawyers that?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISAV SIMIC
utterances.text: Specifically what? Can you please repeat what I said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Ostojic, I'm sorry to interrupt, why don't you ask directly the question to the witness. Just put your question without relying on the proofing note.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Sir, is it correct that you did not know who the officer was that you mentioned on April of 2004 in your Blagojevic case, the officer that you claimed you saw in Bratunac in connection with this convoy?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISAV SIMIC
utterances.text: Yes. I didn't know, and then when I talked with somebody about it later, somebody told me that that was probably Beara whom I didn't know, and I don't know him still to this day.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And at that time, sir, meaning the meeting or the encounter you claim to have had with this officer, you did not ask that officer his name; correct?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISAV SIMIC
utterances.text: No, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And am I also correct, sir, this officer with respect to this encounter again, did not introduce himself; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISAV SIMIC
utterances.text: I didn't ask him and probably the man didn't need to do so because I was agitated and stressed when I met him, and I was probably a little bit curt or impolite with him which is not really my habit and now when I think about it, I'm a little bit embarrassed or ashamed about my behaviour, but that's how it was at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Describe the officer that you claim you saw, sir?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISAV SIMIC
utterances.text: I could easily describe him had I had seen him clearly, but as we say everything had -- all the blood had gone to my eyes, I was angry because I had to intervene, and I was angry thinking about the consequences for Bratunac because of what had been done, so at that time all I could see was the outline of the man and I saw that he was an officer, I was not looking for any soldier but for some superior officer because I wanted to do what the president of the executive board told me to do, person on duty. I don't know if he knew that there would be a senior officer on duty that anyway, I should address that person and just having seen the ranks, I assumed that this was an officer and addressed him impolitely as I already mentioned, but let me finish, please. I didn't remember, I mean, I usually have a very good visual memory, so quite unusually for me, and according to some psychological code, I manage to retain facial lines and after that I'm able to reconstruct some event, but at that time I was not able to see anything characteristic with which I could then describe somebody. And judging by what I have just said, it could only have been the mentioned officer.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Sir, who told you that this person subsequent to that, who told you that it may have been Beara?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISAV SIMIC
utterances.text: This is also difficult for me because later I talked with people in my office because that was something that stayed with me for a long time as some kind of experience of those events, and where I was quite in some enforced stress, excitement, and then somebody just remarked that it could have been only him. I'm not claiming that he claimed and probably he -- he probably said that was probably, but I don't know if it was that man, or I don't know if the person who said that actually had known him. It was unofficial. Sometimes when somebody comes to the office and then we are talking a little bit with a coffee, and so I didn't pay attention, so it wasn't really that important to me who that officer really was, I just retold that as an event that happened to me during those days. So then I just more for the sake of a conversation and for the sake of relief of emotions I told it not because I really wanted to be interested or wished to be interested in who is that officer exactly, I don't know, I have no reason. First of all, I don't know whether he is just an officer on duty or responsible so that I would then show any interest in who he is and how he is performing his duties, what sort of an officer he is, well, I don't want to be bringing any conclusions that would not hold water for anyone.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: When did this all occur, sir? When did you have this discussion as you've just described as length to us?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISAV SIMIC
utterances.text: This could have been in the morning hours, after 8.00 in the morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Who is the person that told you that it may be Beara?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISAV SIMIC
utterances.text: I already said that this was something that happened during a conversation in the office where there were more than one -- there were persons and there was talk, and I just heard that it could have been Beara, probably Beara. Please, this expression probably. This is the answer that I heard to this story of mine, but I didn't pay attention at the time who it was, somebody just interjected that as I was talking.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, one moment, Mr. Ostojic. Mr. Gosnell, transcript problem?

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Your Honour, this is just -- this is an objection perhaps to assist my colleague. I believe there is some ambiguity in the question, line 19 of page 54, when did this all occur. I think there might just be some ambiguity as to what "this" is referring to which might be clarified.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think you are perfectly right.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Sir, did at any time Mr. Deronjic discuss with you Mr. Beara? At any time after July 1995 all throughout the next few years?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISAV SIMIC
utterances.text: Regardless of the fact that we were friends, I spoke very rarely with Deronjic other than before the assembly I didn't interfere in his job, he didn't interfere in mine. At the beginning I said I didn't want anybody to influence my work and if my work is good, there is a assembly, we can discuss that, and I'm going to bear all the consequences. So we didn't really have any need for him to check me or for me to check him. What he is doing -- he is doing what was he was doing, what was given to him to do, and I was doing my own stuff, and I thought that was the best way to know who is what and how.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: With all due respect, I don't know if I really got an answer to my question, but did Mr. Deronjic discuss with you, sir, at any time after July of 1995, Mr. Beara? Yes or no, if I may?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISAV SIMIC
utterances.text: Not with me, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now, I want to direct your attention to the testimony you gave earlier on this year of the 18th of January 2008, page 16, lines 7 through 11. If you just give me a second so I can quote it exactly. But at that time sir, under oath, you said that Deronjic asked you if you remembered an incident or meeting involving Mr. Beara, and you answered by saying you don't remember it and you were asleep in essence. Do you remember giving that testimony earlier this year? And just so the record is clear so my friend's can follow, the transcript from the Bosnian court is broken up into three sections, and each section starts again with page 1, so the page reference is to the second portion of the transcript and that's on page 16, lines 11. Do you remember giving that testimony, sir, in essence?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISAV SIMIC
utterances.text: Thank you for reminding me, but --

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: You are welcome.

utterances.speaker: LJUBISAV SIMIC
utterances.text: What I said just now, what I said is due to the impreciseness of your own question, when. Many months, maybe many years later, at one situation I don't know if I said that also here or in the Blagojevic case, well, it doesn't matter, but I'm going to confirm that -- well, the war was over, and I was no longer at the municipal office, Deronjic I think, was and at one time when we were sitting, having a drink somewhere he asked me laughing at a situation from my work history which was interesting and spicy to him, and I felt uncomfortable about it, and somebody else was with us then, and he said well, imagine I came -- well, allegedly I was sitting in front of the office of the SDS, I don't know there was some kind of a soft chair there and waiting for I don't know who, probably him, I fell asleep. And then when he came in, he woke me up, and he told me that I should go out and come back later if he needs me. I said I don't really remember that. I asked him, are you making this up in order to make a joke in company or what? And he was laughing and he said that this had really happened, but I really then or today, do not happen to remember at all coming back later to talk about something with him. That's what we talked about. I remember that conversation. It was many years later in a cafe while we were having a drink, there was somebody else with us it, and it was more of a joke at my expense that I was fallen asleep in a chair waiting for somebody, actually him, but anyway, he said I was supposed to have a conversation with him and then he woke me up and then sent me away and told me to come back later.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now, I want to ask you, sir, if you stand by your sworn testimony that you gave in the Sarajevo court on the 10th of January 2008, specifically page 15, line 17 through 19 --

utterances.speaker: LJUBISAV SIMIC
utterances.text: I am not looking at the text, but if I said anything in that sense, that is that perhaps it has been interpreted a little bit differently, but the essence is the same, and I stand by the essence that Deronjic told me that he had come and found me in that chair in the condition of sleep and that he woke me up and sent me off to return later and I don't remember that to this day. I tried by some mechanisms to access if I remember any details to see if this could have happened or not, and I thought that Deronjic will -- just made this up in order to make a joke.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: We heard your testimony earlier that you did not have any meetings with Deronjic on the night of the 13th. But I was asking you a different question and trying to conclude part of this. I wanted know if you could confirm this for me, do you stand by your testimony given in the Sarajevo court 10th of January 2008, page 15, line 17 through 19 as follows: You were asked by the Prosecutor, Mr. Alcock there -- line 13, I'm sorry. "May have an answer, please, sir, do you know Colonel Beara." Answer line 14 "No, I'm ready to answer --

utterances.speaker: LJUBISAV SIMIC
utterances.text: Baraga is that it?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Beara?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISAV SIMIC
utterances.text: Oh, I'm sorry it seemed to me as if you had said Baraga. So it is knew name for me, I am sorry I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: That's okay. I may have misspoken regrettably. No the Prosecutor is asking you on line 13 do you know Colonel Beara, you answer on line 14 "No, I'm ready --

utterances.speaker: LJUBISAV SIMIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: To answer your question, what you mentioned that Miroslav stated elsewhere. The next line, sir, judge -- the Honourable Judge Gluhajic asked "the Prosecutor has asked you a question. Do you know Colonel Beara?" Answer by the witness, you, sir. "The answer is no. I've heard about him, but I've never had a chance to see him." Do you stand by that answer --

utterances.speaker: LJUBISAV SIMIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: -- that you gave?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISAV SIMIC
utterances.text: Completely.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now, it goes on to say, sir, at lines 21, although the microphone was not activated for the immediate beginning of the question. It talks about whether or not you had any meetings on the night of the 13th of July with Miroslav Deronjic, and you answer at line 23, "no." Do you stand by that, sir?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISAV SIMIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now, you talked a little bit about the meeting with Deronjic, and I have to ask this you this because during this conversation that Deronjic wanted you to discuss, although you say he was laughing, was he talking about the circumstances when purportedly people were discussing killing Bosnian-Muslims or killing prisoners?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISAV SIMIC
utterances.text: No, he said that we were sitting -- I mean, you don't talk about these things in cafes, neither do you hold meetings in cafes on this topic. I think he just wanted to describe a comical situation from that period, and that's what he told. I was the topic of that comedy. Wasn't anything more than that.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: On the same transcript, same page, just the very next section, the very next line actually the Prosecutor continues to ask you, although again the microphone was not activated, he is discussing circumstances -- and it's line 24 and 25, page 15, then proceeding on the next page, page 16, lines 1 through 11, he asked you about circumstances in any meetings on some other date when he got you out of the room when a soldier was talking too openly or too loudly about killing prisoners. The answer by you, sir. The "No, and this is the reason why I wanted to -- to answer your question." And then the Honourable Judge Gluhajic again intervenes he says, You may answer the question right now. The question was put to you in a different manner. The witness, sir, by you, you state at follows: "Once Miroslav asked me in Bratunac whether -- whether I remember being there and that he came out and I was asleep in -- in the chair and that he said that I should go somewhere else or I should go somewhere and -- but I responded that I do not recall this incident, that I was asleep. So it was not even my subconscious mind."

utterances.speaker: LJUBISAV SIMIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: When did this meeting take place, sir, that you discussed this with Deronjic and that he made fun of you being asleep?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISAV SIMIC
utterances.text: He told me this later in this cafe --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Just one moment. Mr. Gosnell.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Your Honours, I feel as if the same question is being asked in a different glove again and again, and I would suggest to you that the witness has already answered this question at least twice, in fact. So I'm not sure what is being what this document is being used for. Impeachment or confirmation or for what purpose, but I object to the repetition of the same questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, I would like to hear your comments on this, Mr. Ostojic.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I don't have any comment on it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Then please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Sir, could you tell me to the best of your recollection --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And try to move because you had asked for 30 minutes and already you have -- we are not stopping you of course but you are already over one hour.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I appreciate that, but I actually asked for an hour then there was a mistake, and we did reduce it to a half hour, but thank you for your --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Sir, what I want to know as you sit here today has anyone at any time including Mr. Deronjic ever told you to put or place Mr. Beara's name in or around the area of Bratunac as being purportedly there? Did anyone ever tell you that?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISAV SIMIC
utterances.text: I heard a number of times, for example, the president of the executive board said that Beara was in Bratunac. This last example, I'm sure of everything else that we talked about Miroslav and this story of Miroslav to this day, I said that twice just now, and I think that is quite clear. I do not recall that having happened like that. I understood that as Miroslav's joke, as my expense in company to make them laugh. I don't deny it, it's possible that it happened, but I really do not -- and I told Miroslav that really he construed it well, and if it was a joke all right I'm really interest well did this really happen and he just through laughter, he said well, he couldn't remember. I mean, I couldn't remember. I don't to this day haven't managed to remember a single detail. I'm in a dilemma today, did he really make up this as a joke, or did I fall asleep in that situation, I don't recall falling asleep or leaving or even seeing Deronjic at all. I mean, this is it in the briefest possible way. I mean, I don't want to go on about it any more. I don't know if you have any instruments to help me dig this out of my subconscious mind, I have nothing against that, but for all those years ever since Miroslav told me that I've been asking myself if it's possible that I was in that situation and that this happened and it was as comical as it appeared. I mean, it never seemed comical to me, not even now.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Are you familiar or do you know what the relationship was with Dragan Mrkovic and Mr. Borovcanin, if any?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISAV SIMIC
utterances.text: Bratunac is a small town, you know. Everybody knows each other practically. We spent time together. Everybody socialized with everyone else. I mean, what can I conclude on the basis of that socializing. I know why I spent time with certain people, but I never thought about why other people would spend their time with people.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. I'm going to read to you what appears on Exhibit 2D172 and just for the Court and the record, it's a supplemental information sheet. I want to know if you know anything about this in particular, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment, Mr. Simic. Mr. Gosnell.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Your Honours, on Monday we filed a motion that directly concerns what my learned friend is now attempting to do. We strongly object to the use of documents that are not admitted in evidence being put to a witness in order to -- sorry. May I ask the Court to request the witness to remove his head phones.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Right, Mr. Simic, could you remove your headphones, please. Yes, Mr. Gosnell.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: I wouldn't wish to try to recapitulate all the arguments that are in that motion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You don't need to.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Right, but that does state our position. We do believe that that is procedurally improper. I draw the Court's attention to the fact that this isn't even a statement. This is a proofing note prepared by, albeit a very capable and respected member of the Office of the Prosecutor, but nonetheless it's not a statement. And for the reasons more fully set out in the motion, this is highly prejudicial, highly improper and we object to it. And furthermore, Mr. President this links in as well to the grounds for our motion for certification. We are now going beyond, as far as I can tell, what is previously been raised in this case by the Beara Defence in any case, so we also object on that ground.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Gosnell. Mr. McCloskey and then I'll call on you, Mr. Ostojic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I'll try to be brief, but for well over two years we've been going on the practice established by this Court that material for cross-examination was wide open as it should be. There of course can be exceptions we are trying to find out which document he is referring to, but a proofing note of a statement, I can't imagine why that cannot be used. We've read the motion, frankly, it's absurd and has no legal foundation. And goes directly against our over two years of practice on both sides. So I will eventually get what this document is in particular, but as a matter of precedent, I think it's important that people be allowed to use material for cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Leaving we'll now be asking you, Mr. Ostojic, to comment, but would kindly also ask you to leave unprejudiced the merits of the Borovcanin Defence team motion is referred to. That we'll be decided if at all in due course, but for the time being let's deal with this particular document what is your position after having heard both Mr. Gosnell and Mr. McCloskey, Mr. Ostojic?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I certainly think that we are entitled to ask questions --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second, let me be clear, we are talking about Mr. Nicholls proofing note.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Yes, Judge Kwon, I don't know what my learned friend says wasn't he states on page 63 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PROST
utterances.text: Mr. Nicholls' proofing note of?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: His conversation with Momir Nikolic referencing particularly on page 3 Dragan Mrkovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Do you have anything to add?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I was starting to add it, but no I do not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Yes I thought we had concluded, Mr. Gosnell.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: I apologise, I thank you the Court's patience.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You will always find us very patient.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: We do not suggest that my learned friend cannot put a proposition. We fully we discussed that fully in the motion, but I wants to make that clear right now. We don't have a problem with my learned friend putting a proposition. We have a problem with giving it this air of reliability which we believe is improper.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. Yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes. Now that I know what we are talking about, I think that proofing note from anyone involved in this case like this is perfectly open for cross-examination especially for the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ostojic, if you wish to conclude?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I don't have anything.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You don't want the final word. Okay. Thank you. [Trial Chamber confers].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, Mr. McCloskey, sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Just one other point for your information that Momir Nikolic is available to be called in this courtroom as it has to do with information and whether that information is -- should be cross-examined.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Our decision is as follows: I would like first of all to make it clear that what we are deciding now present and will be without prejudice to your motion that you filed earlier on this week which we will deal with after we've heard from the Prosecution and from other colleagues of yours. On this particular occasion, particularly since we are dealing with Momir Nikolic, who was, in part, the subject matter of a previous decision of this Trial Chamber, we think that the best way to proceed, Mr. Ostojic, is for you to put the proposition to the witness one or more as you please, which you may base in your mind on what is contained in this document without, however, making reference to the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I just referenced it so my learned friends can follow along, in case they were wondering where that might come from.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We appreciate that. But in the meantime, you created a problem. We are trying to solve this problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I apologise for that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You don't need to apologise, maybe others would have done exactly the same. But in the meantime, let's proceed along the lines that we have indicated to you, Mr. Ostojic, I'm sure you will agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Sir, given that you just told us on page 62, line 16 that Bratunac is a small town everyone knows each other practically, we spent time together, we socialized, et cetera, et cetera, did you ever hear or come to learn that people were actually lying about Beara's purported involvement of the Bosnian-Muslims in Glogova? Did you ever discuss that with anyone?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISAV SIMIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Did you ever hear from anyone -- sorry. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: LJUBISAV SIMIC
utterances.text: I will be able to assist you immediately to understand fully why I did not. I didn't want to even listen to the rumours that were doing the rounds at that time except to the official meetings, because I knew that testimony would have to be given in court at one point and I didn't want to contaminate my memory of what I myself had seen or heard with what other people had told me. I didn't want to have this confusion in my head. And I didn't take any of those rumours as being credible or in any way important for me. I knew how things are to be done in any serious proceedings, and that's what was important to me. I didn't have the time to or the inclination to listen rumours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ostojic.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I just want to make a comment if I may, I think if we can appreciate the question, I'm not telling him they did testify, I'm inquiring whether or not they testified if he knows. So it's a very open-ended question whether they are protected or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But if he says yes like he did on the previous occasion, then there is a follow-up for which.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I don't know what the answer is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Neither do we. So that's why we have to take precautions. Let's stay in private session while you conclude this series of questions, if you have any more.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We are in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Just if I can follow -up on the officer that you claim you saw on or about the 13th of July 1995, and I know I asked you can you describe him and you gave us a lengthy answer, but do you remember, if at all, sir, if he was your height, shorter or taller than you?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISAV SIMIC
utterances.text: I've already told you about my emotional state at the time, and I have to admit that I did not have any visual capabilities at all. This was just an impression that I was left with and now I could try and extract some things that would not really reflect reality. So I don't want to speculate. Because I know myself or at least it seems to me that I know myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Just give me one moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President, for the additional time, I appreciate it very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you Mr. Ostojic. Ms. Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: In the mean time can you go back to private session briefly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, let's revert to private session for a short while, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, we are back in open session. Ms. Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I don't have any questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Ms. Fauveau. Thank you, Madam Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, five, ten minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Good morning, sir, I'm Natacha Fauveau Ivanovic, and I represent General Miletic, I have a few questions to ask you. When you were president of municipality of Bratunac in 1994, 1995, do you know that the DutchBat which was stationed in the enclave Srebrenica was supplied by the Fontana hotel which is in Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISAV SIMIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I know that quite well.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Therefore you can confirm that indeed the DutchBat obtained certain merchandise from Bratunac, from the hotel.

utterances.speaker: LJUBISAV SIMIC
utterances.text: They obtained the merchandise based on the orders that they gave, it gave, and I think that they went -- their soldiers went to the Fontana hotel every week in order to have some fun, although it just -- it was just a facility that provided accommodation and food, and it didn't have any other programs.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: I would now ask you a few questions concerning the call you gave to the HCR in Belgrade. After this call you gave, did the convoy from HCR arrive in Belgrade?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISAV SIMIC
utterances.text: Yes, it did.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Did this convoy arrive on the same day when you made this call or the next day?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISAV SIMIC
utterances.text: The same day. But there was a delay that I did not expect, I told you already that it was in the early evening. At that time the population that was outside of the DutchBat zone had already been evacuated to they came with me to the gate and they went to the DutchBat base to see what the needs were and where to unload their stuff and where to distribute it. I didn't want to go there again because I had already gone during the day, so they went there on their own.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: When this convoy from the HCR arrived, there was a part of a population which hadn't yet been evacuated, is that so?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISAV SIMIC
utterances.text: That's right. The part of the population that was in the base that was fenced in, it was an area that was used by UNPROFOR. It was a wire fence around it, I don't know what to call it.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Did the representatives of the HCR, were they in a possibility to have a contact with the population waiting to be evacuated?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISAV SIMIC
utterances.text: They could fully because they had gone there unescorted by me and they probably, I assume, that they reported to somebody from the Dutch battalion, and they were able to talk to whoever they wanted up there.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: After during this visit in the DutchBat precinct, did you have an opportunity to spend the evening with a representative of the HCR? We see that in your testimony in the Blagojevic case. These two people from the HCR, did they tell you something about the way the evacuation was organised?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISAV SIMIC
utterances.text: They never told me anything about that, but I saw that they spoke to some reporter in front of the DC warehouse. He saw the trucks pass by and he approached them, but I didn't approach them myself. I didn't want to interfere in any way with the journalist or with this man. I stood at the side and I waited for him to finish. Apart from what I said, apart from what I was told by the UNHCR representative, we didn't discuss it any longer.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Do these two persons did not tell you there was any dearth of anything or something which was not going properly?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISAV SIMIC
utterances.text: They told me that they were sorry they were late. I knew that myself, that what they must have heard up there, but the DutchBat commander says that there was no need for this amount of goods and that they could meet the demands of the population with their own supplies, seeing that the evacuation would be completed tomorrow quite soon, and then this food was surplus, something to that effect.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have no other questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Krgovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Simic, my name is Dragan Krgovic and I'm representing General Gvero and will be asking you just a few questions now. Today in your evidence, answering to the questions asked by my colleague Mr. Gosnell, you said that sometime on the 12th of July in the afternoon together with Mladic you went to Srebrenica; do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISAV SIMIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And you stayed there for about an hour with him?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISAV SIMIC
utterances.text: Yes, about an hour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Did you have an opportunity to go into the town of Srebrenica itself on the 12th?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISAV SIMIC
utterances.text: Well, you cannot get into Srebrenica at all. You had to pass through the whole of the town because there's only one street there. That town has only one street, and there is a very small junction there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And did you linger, did you stay at any of the locations around the town or inside the town?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISAV SIMIC
utterances.text: We stayed for awhile by the department store because I noticed there a journalist, a female journalist, that's what I concluded on the basis of what she was doing she was talking to with two civilians, I think they were Muslims, and Mladic got out and spoke to her while I remained in the car, I was waiting for this to finish.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Let me just clarify for the transcript. The first part of your answer is not clear. When you said that you cannot go into Srebrenica, that means that you actually have to pass through the street and then get to the --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: Could the witness and counsel please make pauses between questions and answers because then we will have no problems for the transcript.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Stop, stop, stop. Mr. Simic, there is a small problem which has been brought about by the fact that both you and Mr. Krgovic speak the same language. You have not allowed sufficient time, sufficient pause after his question for the interpreters to be able to interpret what you were saying. So we have missed completely your answer. When Mr. Krgovic puts a question to you, you need to allow a few seconds before you start answering the question, and then it should be okay. So --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do apologise, I will do my best.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Everyone does it, Mr. Simic. So we are not blaming you at all. The question was, "let me just clarify for the transcript, the first part of your answer is not clear when you said that you cannot go into Srebrenica, that means that you actually have to pass through the street and then get to the --"

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And then you come to this junction?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISAV SIMIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. And you also allow for a short pause, Mr. Krgovic. Thank you, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: I'll do my best.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But the thing is this, now he said just yes, and it was before I recall hearing him speak for at least 6, 7, 8, 10 seconds. So what was he saying before?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: I'll ask the witness to repeat.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Your answer to the same question before when I stopped you was much longer than the yes that you have just spoken now.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Perhaps I can assist by describing it now. So if you want to get to the centre of the town, there is only one street leading from the direction of Bratunac, and then you have to pass through more than half of the town because Srebrenica has only one street. It's some kind of a stream or a creek. And it's kind of like a gully, and there's not much space for buildings to be put up. It just goes, there's this one street that it goes through this gully where Srebrenica is. And by the time we got to the department store, we had already passed through more than half of the town itself. That was the essence. So as we went by this street to the department store, we passed through more than half of the town, and that was the only road that we could take from Bratunac in the direction of Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Simic, where did you go from that junction?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISAV SIMIC
utterances.text: We went on taking the same street from that junction. I can mention some of the buildings that we passed, the municipality assembly, the court, the culture hall, and since the general wanted to go to Banja Guber. Because he had heard about it, he had never been there and he wanted to see the spring for this water, he asked me if I could show him the way and take them to the spring. So we are heading towards the Banja Guber spring which is outside of the city limits, so we passed through the whole town. We passed by the last buildings on our way to where this healing water spring is used, this water is -- there is this building, this was operational before the war. At any rate, he wanted to check what the situation was there, whether could be made operational again. So we went on to Banja Guber and there was a spring by the side of the road that's not the main spring but it is used generally by the people, people could bathe themselves in it. That's what people did because there were all kinds of beliefs what good it does to you. So we stopped there, and then when we went further on, the road was damaged because of the rains, and the stones that were used to pave the road were all over the place, so we had -- and there was a tree, so we had to remove the obstacles. And then we went to the level ground from which you can see the spring because the spring is to a side, it's a hilly area. The road leads right into the hills. So we went to this building which was used for recreational purposes. You could have a drink there, tourists walked, used to walk all the way up there, and then walk down to their hotel, wherever it was that they stayed during the cures. And then we went up to the level ground to the platform, I showed him where the spring was, but he didn't go to the springs, we just turned around and went back.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: So, in fact, you toured the whole of Srebrenica on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISAV SIMIC
utterances.text: Yes, more or less the whole of Srebrenica. There was this area in direction of Jadar that we didn't go to, but you can see this area towards Jadar when you turn towards Guber from the culture hall, so the whole town was in our field of vision. We could see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Simic, can you tell us what condition were the buildings in the town itself of Srebrenica? Did you notice anything strange, the impact sites, signs of shelling?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISAV SIMIC
utterances.text: Well, the road was passable, it was dirty, as dirty as the roads were during the war because it was difficult to clean them. The only difference was that Srebrenica was different because there was a lot of wood that was used for fuel, wood piles in front of the houses. It looked like a huge wood shed. And it would be quite difficult to actually move around the town for pedestrians and for cars to move around because of that. Had the traffic been any heavier, but I found it quite surprising, and I was quite pleased with it that there was not so much consequences of the shelling. If I thought that there would be stray dogs who might be hit with something in the heavy fighting and it was high summer, and I was quite pleasantly surprised that I didn't see any of it. And Srebrenica looked like a normal town, only it was abandoned. It was empty. There were no people. Just the two civilians that I described to you that the journalist, the female journalist was talking to.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Did you notice any damage to the buildings that you mentioned, the municipality building, the hospital, the culture hall?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISAV SIMIC
utterances.text: Well, the hospital is to the left. As we passed by we could only see the wall and the roof. You could not see any damage. You could not see any signs that it had been torched or looted. It looked like it used to look before. As for the buildings up there, you could see that there was some damage caused in the fighting earlier on because of the time and the atmosphere, you could see that shell had fallen here or there, but you could see that this was all the damage. It changed colour. I could see in the Bratunac what it looks like when a shell impacts, and quite to my surprise, I didn't notice any of it as we passed through Srebrenica. I had thought since there had been fighting, that there would be chaos and that it would be bad in the streets. That's why I was not really so happy when general invited me to go with him.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Did you have an opportunity to pass by the UNPROFOR base in the town of Srebrenica itself?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISAV SIMIC
utterances.text: Yes, I think that the base was somewhere close to the city cemetery, I think further in the front.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Krgovic, I have to stop you there. We need to evacuate the building. We need to evacuate the building, we've just been informed that, the Court room and the building, so we'll have the break now in any case. But you will have to evacuate the building as per instructions that were circulated before. We will reconvene, if at all, after the drill is over.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: 12.26 to be reconvened on Thursday, the 23rd day of October, 2008, at 9.00 a.m.
